casadio_morasso_sanguineti_2005.cite: Casadio M, Morasso PG, Sanguineti V (2005). Direct measurement of ankle stiffness during quiet standing: implications for control modelling and clinical application. Gait Posture 21(4):410-24.
casadio_morasso_sanguineti_2005.verified_via: NCBI esummary + efetch abstract, live this session
casadio_morasso_sanguineti_2005.numbers: intrinsic ankle stiffness = 64 +/- 8% of critical, via motorised footplate + 1-degree step disturbances (EMG-checked to exclude reflex contamination), independent lab/method/decade from Loram & Lakie. Framed by the authors as the lower bound of a real range (91% = upper bound, smaller test disturbance); both bounds are sub-critical.
casadio_morasso_sanguineti_2005.role: forced adversary for the passive-insufficiency claim -- an independent measurement that COULD have pushed stiffness toward/above criticality instead reinforces insufficiency at an even lower value

horak_nashner_1986.cite: Horak FB, Nashner LM (1986). Central programming of postural movements: adaptation to altered support-surface configurations. J Neurophysiol 55(6):1369-81.
horak_nashner_1986.verified_via: NCBI esummary + efetch abstract, live this session
horak_nashner_1986.numbers: Ankle strategy (normal support surface): 73-110ms EMG latency, distal-to-proximal muscle activation, produces ankle torque. Hip strategy (support surface short relative to foot length): same latencies, proximal-to-distal (opposite) activation, little/no ankle torque, produces horizontal shear force. Intermediate surface lengths -> complex combined patterns.

runge_shupert_horak_zajac_1999.cite: Runge CF, Shupert CL, Horak FB, Zajac FE (1999). Ankle and hip postural strategies defined by joint torques. Gait Posture 10(2):161-70.
runge_shupert_horak_zajac_1999.verified_via: NCBI esummary + efetch abstract, live this session
runge_shupert_horak_zajac_1999.numbers: Backward flat-surface translations swept 5-55 cm/s: hip flexor torque ADDS to ankle plantarflexor torque as velocity increases (a continuum). 'Hip torque without accompanying ankle torque (pure hip strategy) was not observed.'
runge_shupert_horak_zajac_1999.independent_variable: translation velocity on a FIXED flat surface
runge_shupert_horak_zajac_1999.role: forced adversary of the naive 'three discrete strategy boxes' reading -- partially falls (real continuum, not discrete), refining rather than simply confirming the brief's hierarchy framing

mcilroy_maki_1996.cite: McIlroy WE, Maki BE (1996). Age-related changes in compensatory stepping in response to unpredictable perturbations. J Gerontol A Biol Sci Med Sci 51(6):M289-96.
mcilroy_maki_1996.verified_via: NCBI esummary + efetch abstract, live this session
mcilroy_maki_1996.numbers: n=14 (5 young 22-28y, 9 elderly 65-81y), 600ms platform translations. 98% of all trials required stepping at all. Elderly needed multiple/additional steps in 63% of trials vs young, described as 'twice as likely' (implies young ~31%, derived from the stated ratio -- not printed verbatim in the abstract, flagged honest).
mcilroy_maki_1996.role: third (stepping) strategy tier + age-linked deficit exactly where ankle+hip torque is exhausted

prieto_1996.cite: Prieto TE, Myklebust JB, Hoffmann RG, Lovett EG, Myklebust BM (1996). Measures of postural steadiness: differences between healthy young and elderly adults. IEEE Trans Biomed Eng 43(9):956-66.
prieto_1996.verified_via: NCBI esummary + efetch abstract, live this session
prieto_1996.numbers: n=20 healthy young (21-35y) vs n=20 healthy elderly (66-70y), EO/EC quiet stance. Mean COP velocity was the ONLY measure identifying age-related changes in both eye conditions AND EO/EC differences in both groups.
prieto_1996.role: independent, cross-decade convergence with the internal ORG-POSTURAL-BALANCE cell's own metric-specificity finding (velocity carries the signal, RMS/area do not)

maki_holliday_topper_1994.cite: Maki BE, Holliday PJ, Topper AK (1994). A prospective study of postural balance and risk of falling in an ambulatory and independent elderly population. J Gerontol 49(2):M72-84.
maki_holliday_topper_1994.verified_via: NCBI esummary + efetch abstract, live this session
maki_holliday_topper_1994.numbers: n=100 (age 62-96), 1-year prospective fall monitoring. Lateral spontaneous-sway amplitude (eyes-closed) = single best predictor of future falling, moderate accuracy, predictive even in subjects with no recent fall history.

fernie_1982.cite: Fernie GR, Gryfe CI, Holliday PJ, Llewellyn A (1982). The relationship of postural sway in standing to the incidence of falls in geriatric subjects. Age Ageing 11(1):11-6.

new_computation_this_session.description: Passive-only (no delay, no active gain) inverted-pendulum stability check: I*theta''=(mgh-Kp_passive)*theta, characteristic roots +/-omega, omega=sqrt((mgh-Kp_passive)/I). Real positive omega = unconditional exponential instability. Uses ONLY numbers already verified in this repo's own JSON (mass, height, mgh) plus the two independently live-verified stiffness fractions above -- no new simulation, six lines of stdlib Python, shown in the doc's Repro section.
new_computation_this_session.pre_registered_threshold: Kp_passive/mgh < 1.0 required for a real (unstable) root
new_computation_this_session.verdict: Both independent measurements give Kp_passive/mgh<1.0 (0.91, 0.64), both give a real positive omega, both predict collapse within 2-4 seconds under passive stiffness alone with zero active correction -- far short of real quiet standing's minutes-long duration. The forced adversary (an independent, differently-parametrized measurement that could have rescued passive-sufficiency) instead reinforces insufficiency at an even lower stiffness fraction.

strategy_hierarchy_verdict.claim: ankle -> hip -> step strategy transition as perturbation/task magnitude increases
strategy_hierarchy_verdict.evidence: Horak & Nashner 1986 (surface-geometry variable) + Runge et al 1999 (translation-velocity variable, forced adversary test of discreteness) + McIlroy & Maki 1996 (third/stepping tier, age-linked)
strategy_hierarchy_verdict.refinement: the brief's 'hierarchy' framing is refined, not simply confirmed: Runge et al 1999's own explicit test found hip torque always ADDS to (never replaces) ankle torque on a flat surface across a 5-55cm/s velocity sweep -- a continuum, not 3 discrete boxes. Surface geometry (Horak & Nashner) is a separate, additional constraint that CAN force a sharp ankle-torque cutoff. Discreteness is constraint-dependent, not perturbation-size-dependent alone.
